_comment: User-editable anti-pattern rules for pre-tool-course-correct.py. Set enabled=false to disable a rule.

rules.description: Use the Grep tool instead of grep/rg in Bash
rules.message: Use the Grep tool instead. Example: Grep(pattern='<your pattern>', path='<dir or file>'). Pipelines (`| grep`) are allowed and auto-rewritten to rg.

rules.description: Use the Read tool instead of sed -n for line-range reads
rules.message: Use Read(file_path='<path>', offset=N, limit=N) instead of sed -n for line-range reads.

rules.description: Use the Read tool instead of cat for reading files
rules.message: Use the Read tool. Example: Read(file_path='<path>'). Heredocs and pipelines are allowed.

rules.description: Prefer temp file input over heredoc payloads for structured command inputs
rules.message: Avoid large heredoc command payloads. Write payloads to a temp file and pass them into the command via file argument or stdin redirection so content is versionable and reusable.

rules.description: Use the Read tool with offset/limit instead of head/tail
rules.message: Use Read(file_path='<path>', offset=N, limit=N) or `tail` in pipelines. `tail -f` is allowed.

rules.description: Use the Glob tool instead of find for file discovery
rules.message: Use the Glob tool. Example: Glob(pattern='**/*.rs', path='<dir>'). Use find only for -exec/-delete/-mtime.
Use `bun`/`bunx`. Examples: `bun install`, `bun run build`, `bunx tsc`.

rules.description: Use mise instead of nvm for Node.js version management
Use uv instead of pip/pip3 for package management
Do not sleep or use timeout as a wait — find productive work or use run_in_background
rules.message: Do not sleep or wrap commands in timeout as a wait mechanism. If waiting for a background task, use `run_in_background` — you will be notified when it completes. If polling, run the check command directly (e.g. `gh run view`). If blocked, find other productive work to do.

rules.description: Use the Glob tool instead of ls for directory listing
rules._todo: comment-false-positive: add '^\\s*#' exception to stop comment lines like '# ls foo' from firing this rule. Same fix needed for no-cat-use-read. Implement once confirmed the rules engine matches full command string including leading whitespace.
rules.message: Use the Glob tool for file discovery. Example: Glob(pattern='*', path='<dir>') or Glob(pattern='**/*.rs'). Glob returns sorted results with no token overhead from formatting.

rules.description: Use the Edit tool instead of sed for in-place file edits
rules.message: Use the Edit tool for file modifications. Example: Edit(file_path='<path>', old_string='...', new_string='...'). Edit provides better diffing, review, and undo. Piped sed for text transformation is fine.

rules.description: Wrap Bash-specific syntax in `nu -c` for execution
rules.message:
Wrap this in `nu -c "..."`. All Bash tool calls must use Nushell. Example: Bash(nu -c "<command>").

Common nu rewrites:
  cmd 2>&1 | tail -N  →  nu -c "do { cmd } | complete | get stdout | lines | last N | str join \"\\n\""
  cmd 2>&1 | head -N  →  nu -c "do { cmd } | complete | get stdout | lines | first N | str join \"\\n\""
  cmd | grep pattern  →  use the Grep tool, or: nu -c "do { cmd } | complete | get stdout | lines | where { |l| $l =~ 'pattern' } | str join \"\\n\""
  cmd1 && cmd2        →  nu -c "cmd1; cmd2"
  cmd | python3 -c "import json..."  →  nu -c "cmd | from json | ..."

rules.description: Use the Edit tool instead of python3 for file modifications
rules.message: Use the Edit tool for file modifications. Example: Edit(file_path='<path>', old_string='...', new_string='...'). Python file I/O bypasses review, diffing, and undo. For JSON processing, use `nu -c` with `from json`.

rules.description: Do not pass multiple --path flags to cargo install
rules.message: cargo install only accepts one --path. Run separate commands: `cargo install --path crates/foo` then `cargo install --path crates/bar`.

rules.description: Do not cd — use absolute paths or git -C instead
rules.message: Prefer no `cd` in orchestration commands. Use absolute paths, `git -C <path> ...` for repo operations, and tool `path` parameters (Glob/Read/etc.) instead. If a single command chain must change directory for multiple mixed commands, rewrite it as one explicit command sequence and add justification in the task notes.
